title: AA Batteries 8-pack

drivers.name: Store closure (Monday)
drivers.evidence: Store closed Monday for renovation. Past closures reduce sales; this is a known demand reducer.

drivers.name: Price increase (5.5% vs regular)
drivers.evidence: Past weeks with price at $10.81 (5.5% above $10.25) show median x0.94 vs baseline. Noise-adjusted estimate supports ~6% lift down.

adjustment.analysis: The store closure on Monday reduces expected sales. No events or promotions are scheduled. The price is 5.5% above regular, which historically reduces demand. Past price increases (e.g., 2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) show median x0.94 vs baseline. The closure is a known demand reducer; the price increase is a consistent downside driver. Evidence is moderate (two past price spikes, one closure). The classical model ignores these, so we adjust downward. The baseline already includes seasonal and trend signals. Noise-adjusted price effect is x0.94.

brief:
PRODUCT: AA Batteries 8-pack | category Household | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-08 (4 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 10.81 (+5.5% vs regular price 10.25)
  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 35.0 | 5%-95%: 18.9 - 57.9 | 10%-90%: 21.2 - 54.9

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-44% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
